children: Rush Enterprises’ third-quarter revenue and earnings increased year over year, as stronger new commercial vehicle demand—particularly from over-the-road customers amid improved freight rates—and dealership acquisitions lifted sales. Gross margin declined amid a greater mix of lower-margin truck sales and national-account aftermarket business; lower net interest expense also supported results.
¹ Reported as “Total revenue”. ² Reported as “Net income attributable to Rush Enterprises, Inc.”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.
: New and used commercial vehicle revenue rose 16.7%; new heavy-duty unit sales increased 24.2% to 3,994.
: Aftermarket Products and Services revenue increased 5.8% to $679.9M, driven by customer demand and ten dealership acquisitions in June.
: Gross margin fell to 18.3% from 19.9%, reflecting higher truck and national-account sales; aftermarket margin declined to 35.8% from 37.2%.
: Commercial vehicle order backlog was approximately $1,490.1M on September 30, 2026, compared with $647.6M a year earlier.
